bettacraft.configuration.angelfishPreyPe: Small fish (neons, embers, mosquito rasboras ...) and shrimp one adult angelfish eats per day; plants hide them (0 = never)

bettacraft.configuration.animationDistan: Fish further away than this (blocks) are not animated

bettacraft.configuration.autoDetect: Find other water plants by themselves

bettacraft.configuration.badBelow.toolti: Below this water quality bettas are stressed (like by a wrong temperature)
bettacraft.configuration.barbsAndLoaches: Barbs and loaches: tiger, odessa and cherry barb, dwarf chain loach, reticulated loach and garra at the wandering trader, in the aquarium net and wild (off: no new ones; fish already caught stay)
bettacraft.configuration.baseDeclinePerD: Water quality lost per in-game day in every tank, even without animals (0.01 = 1%)
bettacraft.configuration.beautifulWildCh: Chance that a wild animal (spawned in the world or caught with the net) shows a bred colour openly; most are wild-coloured, some carry a bred colour hidden
bettacraft.configuration.behaviour.toolt: Fry and eggs eaten, shoals, bettas, snails, food at the bottom, stocking, catching
bettacraft.configuration.bettaAggression: How hard male bettas go for male guppies and dwarf gouramis (hit points per day; 0 = peaceful)
bettacraft.configuration.bettasHuntShrim: Whether bettas hunt young shrimp and crayfish (plants and Java moss hide them)
bettacraft.configuration.bigAnimalWeight: Spawn weight of the wild big animals (giant catfish, sharks, rays) in their biomes per weight point of the species; they also need deep water and few of their kind nearby (bigAnimalRules.*); 0 disables them (features.bigAnimals)
bettacraft.configuration.bigAnimals.tool: Big animals: giant catfish, sharks, rays and the vanilla dolphin in big tanks by the size rule (bigAnimalRules.*), the large net, the transport tub and the steel leader, wild big animals (off: none go into tanks, no new ones from the wild; those in tanks stay)
bettacraft.configuration.bigContainers: Several animals per bucket and bag
bettacraft.configuration.bigContainers.t: Several animals of one species per bucket and fish bag by their size (a bucket: 32 shrimp, 24 rasboras, 1 betta; a bag half of that), small animals also in a plain bucket (off: one fish per bucket, bags as before)
bettacraft.configuration.bigCrayfish.too: Big crayfish: the Florida crayfish (wild, blue, orange) and the marbled crayfish (only females, multiplies on its own) at the wandering trader, in the aquarium net and wild; they eat plants, dig them up and catch slow fish and small animals (off: no new ones; those in tanks stay)
bettacraft.configuration.bigCrayfishFish: Fish a big crayfish goes for
Fish one big crayfish goes for per day: it eats fry and young fish and small bottom fish, and pinches bettas and other slow fish resting near the floor (plants hide them; 0 = never)
bettacraft.configuration.bigCrayfishPlan: Plants one big crayfish damages per day: it eats a grown plant back by a stage or digs a young rooted plant out of the substrate (epiphytes and moss on wood and stone are safe; 0 = never)
bettacraft.configuration.bigCrayfishPrey: Small animals a big crayfish catches
Small animals (shrimp, small snails, dwarf crayfish) one big crayfish (Florida, marbled) catches per day; plants, moss and shelters hide them (0 = never)
bettacraft.configuration.bigMaxSizeX.too: Maximum tank size along X with features.bigTanks (the larger of this and tank.maxSizeX applies)
bettacraft.configuration.bigMaxSizeY.too: Maximum tank size along Y with features.bigTanks (the larger of this and tank.maxSizeY applies)
bettacraft.configuration.bigMaxSizeZ.too: Maximum tank size along Z with features.bigTanks (the larger of this and tank.maxSizeZ applies)
Chance that a spawn of a wild big animal that passed all other rules really happens (keeps them rare)
bettacraft.configuration.bigTanks.toolti: Big tanks: up to bigTankRules.bigMaxSize* blocks (32 x 16 x 32), with a smaller interior scale (8 or 4) from bigTankRules.interiorScale8Above (off: tank.maxSize* as before; big tanks already built stay)
bettacraft.configuration.bigWildNearby.t: Wild big animals only spawn while fewer than this many of them live within 64 blocks (0 = none spawn)
bettacraft.configuration.bioCo2Bubbles.t: Bubbles per second of a bio CO2 bottle at its best (it starts slowly, varies and fades at the end)
bettacraft.configuration.bioCo2Days.tool: Days a bio CO2 bottle with four sugar ferments (less sugar: shorter)
bettacraft.configuration.biofilmPerWater: Food (portions per day) one water block grows on its own for the small animals
bettacraft.configuration.bothBadMultipli: Speed multiplier of all health timers while two or more conditions (food, temperature, stocking) are bad
bettacraft.configuration.bottleCuttingCh: Chance that filling a glass bottle with swamp water also brings up a cutting (Cryptocoryne, Ludwigia, Rotala)
bettacraft.configuration.bottleDaphniaCh: Chance that a bottle of swamp water brings up a few daphnia as well
bettacraft.configuration.bottleDuckweedC: Chance that filling a glass bottle with swamp water also brings up duckweed
bettacraft.configuration.bottomFoodShare: Chance that a bottom fish gets its share of food that sinks past faster fish; algae wafers go to the bottom fish directly
bettacraft.configuration.breakProtection: Break protection switch in the tank menu: nobody can break a protected tank, its lid, light, feeders and the cabinet below (off: the switch is hidden and does nothing)
bettacraft.configuration.breeding.toolti: Breeding in Bettacraft tanks: conditioning, bubble nest, spawning, eggs and fry

bettacraft.configuration.breedingBoxCapa: Young livebearers that fit into a breeding box
bettacraft.configuration.broodDefence.to: How hard cichlid parents drive other fish away from their eggs and young (hit points per day; 0 = they only chase)

Setting in the cabinet menu: on which tank wall the hose of the external filter in the cabinet goes up (back, left, right, front); jet, bubbles and the current follow it, in front of the outlet the water moves faster (seahorses, corals) (off: always the back wall, the current evenly like before)

bettacraft.configuration.calciumPerMl.to: Calcium (mg/L in one water block) one mL of calcium solution adds (a bigger tank needs more)
bettacraft.configuration.calciumPerStage: Calcium (mg/L in one water block) a stony coral uses per growth stage; in bigger tanks it is shared by more water
bettacraft.configuration.canisterMl.tool: mL of solution in one canister of the dosing pump
bettacraft.configuration.carbonBlocks.to: Water blocks a chamber with activated carbon keeps clean (it is used up, not cleaned)
bettacraft.configuration.caridina.toolti: Caridina bee shrimp (Crystal Red, Crystal Black, Taiwan bees, Tiger) for soft water, with their banding grades (off: no new ones from the net, the wild and the trader; those in tanks stay)
bettacraft.configuration.ceramicBlocks.t: Water blocks a chamber with ceramic rings (bacteria) keeps clean
bettacraft.configuration.cichlids.toolti: Cichlids: ram, Bolivian ram, cockatoo and Agassiz's dwarf cichlid, angelfish and discus at the wandering trader, in the aquarium net and wild (open brooders and cave brooders that guard their brood; off: no new ones; fish already caught stay)
bettacraft.configuration.cleanerStrength: How much algae snails and shrimp graze (1 = normal)
bettacraft.configuration.clipOnFeeder.to: Clip-on feeder: a small automatic feeder that hangs on the side of the glass (for tanks whose top is taken by a light) (off: it cannot be placed and placed ones do not feed)

bettacraft.configuration.clutchSpeed.too: How fast eggs and larvae develop (2 = twice as fast; corydoras eggs need 1.5 days at 1)

mg/L per day a densely planted tank in strong light takes up

bettacraft.configuration.combat.tooltip: Fights between males and predators (#bettacraft:predators) in tanks
bettacraft.configuration.communityFish.t: More community fish: zebra danio, celestial pearl danio, forktail and neon dwarf rainbowfish, emperor, rummy-nose and black phantom tetra, black molly and swordtail at the wandering trader, in the aquarium net and wild (off: no new ones; fish already caught stay)
bettacraft.configuration.conditioningDay: Days a betta stays conditioned (ready for breeding sooner) after a portion of live food
Connected glass textures on textured tanks: the frame of the glass texture only along the outer edges of the whole tank (off: every block shows its own frame)
Degrees the water change must cool the tank by to set the corydoras off

bettacraft.configuration.coolerFePerBloc: FE per tick a cooler needs for each water block it cools (only while it cools)
bettacraft.configuration.coralGrowthSpee: How fast the corals grow (1 = normal, 0 = they do not grow)
bettacraft.configuration.cornerFilterBlo: Water blocks one corner filter keeps clean

bettacraft.configuration.cylinderBubbleD: Days a full CO2 cylinder lasts at one bubble per second

bettacraft.configuration.daphniaRoom.too: Portions of daphnia a full barrel holds
bettacraft.configuration.daysPerYear.too: In-game days per year (Serene Seasons default: 96)

bettacraft.configuration.declinePerOverf: Water quality lost per water block for each portion a fish gets that is not hungry (fed again within half a day)
bettacraft.configuration.decorEffects.to: Almond leaves and alder cones on the floor of a tank interior give off tannins (lower the pH a little) and feed the shrimp; clay and terracotta (tubes, caves, dragon stone) hide young shrimp (off: they are only decoration)

bettacraft.configuration.dolphinHungryDa: Days a dolphin in a tank goes without raw fish (fed by hand) before it starts to lose health
bettacraft.configuration.eggStocking.too: How much of a fish one egg in the bubble nest counts for the stocking (0 = not at all)
bettacraft.configuration.eggsEatenPerDay: How fast the adults eat eggs they can reach (scattered eggs, eggs on the glass); a spawning mop and dense plants protect them (0 = never)

bettacraft.configuration.feederVolume.to: Volume of the feeder clicks from 0 to 1

bettacraft.configuration.filterEfficienc: Share of the waste that a filter removes when it is large enough for the tank
Oxygen exchange of one motor filter (its outlet moves the surface), in water blocks per day

bettacraft.configuration.filterRequiresE: Filters only clean the water while the tank has enough FE
bettacraft.configuration.filterVolume.to: Volume of the filters (external, cabinet, internal, corner filter) from 0 to 1
bettacraft.configuration.finNipping.tool: How hard fin nippers (puffers, tiger barbs) go for long-finned fish (bettas, angelfish, male guppies, gouramis; hit points per day; 0 = never)
bettacraft.configuration.fishBag.tooltip: Fish bag recipe: AUTO = plastic if #bettacraft:plastic_sheets is not empty, otherwise dried kelp; KELP or PLASTIC force one
bettacraft.configuration.fishingChance.t: Chance that fishing in a swamp or mangrove swamp brings up a floating plant instead of the catch

bettacraft.configuration.fishingPlantsRi: Plants fishing brings up in rivers (plantFishingChance): entries "plant_id=weight"; empty = none

Volume of the flow pumps from 0 to 1

Chance that a slow seahorse gets its share of the food while fast fish are in the tank

info.bettacraft.acropora:
Stony coral (SPS): a bush of thin blue-violet branches with pale tips; the most demanding coral.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: strong, flow: strong, needs calcium and clean water.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), rarely a piece from the aquarium net on a reef, or from vanilla corals.
info.bettacraft.activated_carbon: Filter medium (chemical): 16 water blocks per chamber. Used up after a while: replace it. Smelted from charcoal.
info.bettacraft.active_soil:
Substrate for soft water: sneak + right-click an interior floor block with it.
It pulls the pH towards 6.2, softens the water and slowly takes up minerals: just right for bee shrimp. Freshwater plants grow up to a quarter faster on it. It keeps working, it never wears out.
Plain soil (dirt, mud ...) works only half as strongly.
info.bettacraft.air_hose: Crafting part of the air pump. Made from dried kelp or slime balls.
info.bettacraft.air_pump:
Place it next to a tank or on it: its air hose goes into the water. It drives the air stones and sponge filters in the tank interior (4 at full strength; more share the air).
Right-click or sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator (less air, quieter). With power mods and aeration.airPumpRequiresEnergy it needs 2 FE/t per air stone.
info.bettacraft.air_stone:
Place it in a tank interior. While an air pump at the tank drives it, a column of bubbles rises to the surface and brings oxygen into the water (and drives out CO2).
Right-click or sneak + mouse wheel: power regulator.
info.bettacraft.alder_cone:
Dried alder cone: like an almond leaf with a third of the tannins, it lowers the pH a little.
Right-click a tank to put it in, or lay it on the floor of a tank interior: there it keeps giving off tannins and the shrimp graze on it.
Dry birch leaves in a smoker, furnace or on a campfire.
info.bettacraft.algae_scraper:
Cleans algae off the inside of the glass of a tank. Right-click a glass face: that face is clean; sneak + right-click: the whole side of the tank.
Wears a little for every face it cleans.
Algae grow with light, waste in the water and time; snails (nerites best) and shrimp keep them down.
Craft: an iron ingot on two sticks.
info.bettacraft.algae_wafer:
Sinking algae wafer: only the bottom fish (corydoras, plecos, otocinclus, loaches) and the small animals eat it, the bettas and the midwater fish do not get it.
Crafted from dried kelp and betta pellets.
info.bettacraft.alkalinity_canister:
Alkalinity (KH) solution for the dosing pump. Stony corals use it together with the calcium; it also holds the pH of salt water up.
Below 6 dKH they slow down, below 3 they stop.
info.bettacraft.almond_leaf:
Dried catappa leaf: its tannins lower the pH a little (blackwater) and fade within about a week.
One leaf per water block colours the water fully.
Laid on the floor of a tank interior it keeps giving off tannins (about half as many) and the shrimp graze on it.
Dry jungle leaves in a smoker, furnace or on a campfire.
info.bettacraft.alternanthera_reineckii:
A stem plant with deep red leaves; needs strong light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 3.5 days to full size with strong light (a lit tank light), nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: the aquarium net in swamps, jungle water and rivers, rarely fishing in swamps, the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.amazon_frogbit:
A floating plant with round leaves and long roots hanging into the water. Males like to build their bubble nest under a cluster of frogbit most of all.
Grows with light and nutrients, forms offshoots and takes up waste.
Find it: the wandering trader sells it, fishing in swamps.
Take plants out: right-click the surface with an empty hand or an aquarium net; net + sneak thins the whole tank out by half.
info.bettacraft.amazon_sword:
A large rosette of long, sword-shaped leaves: the centre piece of a big tank.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate (the interior floor with a substrate, sand, gravel or dirt). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 7 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: the aquarium net in jungle water (sometimes in rivers), rarely fishing in jungles, the wandering trader; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.anubias_barteri_round_le:
Large, almost round leaves on long stalks; grows very slowly.
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 28 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in jungles, sometimes the aquarium net in jungle water; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Break a rhizome piece to divide it (half of it as an item).

info.bettacraft.aponogeton_ulvaceus:
Long, light green, undulate leaves from a tuber; grown up it raises a flower spike to the surface.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 6 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in rivers, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out.
info.bettacraft.artemia_culture: Hatches into artemia nauplii after one in-game day, but only in light (level 9 or more).
info.bettacraft.artemia_cysts:
Dried brine shrimp eggs, a rare find when you mine sand.
One jar lasts for 16 hatcheries. Jars stack (16 by default, the server can allow 32 or 64); only jars with the same uses left stack together.
info.bettacraft.artemia_hatchery:
Hatches artemia nauplii in the light (level 9 or more).
Pour in salt water bottles, add artemia cysts and glass bottles (also by hopper; emptied salt water bottles are reused).
A batch takes 1 day. Take the nauplii with an empty hand or let a hopper below take them.
info.bettacraft.artemia_nauplii: Food for fry in the second half of the fry stage. One bottle feeds 20 fry.
info.bettacraft.bacopa_caroliniana:
Thick, round leaves on sturdy stems; the tips turn copper under strong light.
Plant it in a tank interior on substrate; grows up to the water surface. From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 4 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: fishing in swamps, sometimes the aquarium net in swamps; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Full-grown it forms side shoots; at the surface it shades the tank.
info.bettacraft.betta_bucket:
A betta in a bucket. Use it on a tank to put the fish in (adds 1000 mB water), or on water to release it.
Catch bettas in swamps with a water bucket or a fish bag.
info.bettacraft.betta_pellets:
Everyday food: one pellet feeds up to 4 bettas (juveniles and older).
Right-click a tank with it or put it into a feeder.
info.bettacraft.betta_spawn_egg: Spawns a betta with random domestic genes.
info.bettacraft.bio_co2:
Place it next to a tank or on it. Fill it: a water bucket, up to four sugar, then yeast.
It ferments for about four days (less sugar: shorter) and gives about one bubble per second - weak and uneven, day and night.
When it is spent, set it up again. Needs no power. Sneak + empty hand: pour it out.
info.bettacraft.breeding_box:
Right-click a tank to hang the breeding box inside the front glass. Young guppies, endlers and platys born while it hangs there fall into it and are safe from the adults; once they are juveniles they swim out.
At most 20 young (config tankmates.breeding.breedingBoxCapacity). Take it out in the tank menu (breeding tab); the young in it swim free.
info.bettacraft.bubble_tip_anemone:
Anemone (Entacmaea quadricolor): tentacles with bubble tips; the home of the clownfish, who lay their eggs at its foot.
On reef rock in a reef tank. Light: medium, flow: medium.
Frag it with shears; wild colonies grow on the warm ocean reefs (shears cut frags off them), more frags from the aquarium net on a reef, vanilla corals or the wandering trader.
info.bettacraft.bucephalandra_blue:
Dark leaves with a bluish shimmer.
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 22 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in jungles and rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Break a rhizome piece to divide it (half of it as an item).

A small Bucephalandra; its tiny leaves turn pink only under strong light (best an LED panel or a high-power LED).
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 22 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.

Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Break a rhizome piece to divide it (half of it as an item).

Greenish leaves that turn white and pink only under strong light (best an LED panel or a high-power LED).

Also sold as 'Biblis': greenish leaves that turn almost white only under strong light (best an LED panel or a high-power LED).
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 26 days to full size with medium light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
Find it: rarely when fishing in rivers; cuttings from trimming.
Shears: trim it (cuttings), inside or from outside on the tank where you look. Break the root: take the whole plant out. Break a rhizome piece to divide it (half of it as an item).
info.bettacraft.bucephalandra_theia:
Bright green, slightly wavy leaves on a compact rhizome.
Plant it in a tank interior on stone or wood (rocks, roots, decoration). From a cutting it grows into a plant of many blocks, about 20 days to full size with little light, nutrients (waste in the water) and 20-30 °C, also while nobody is inside.
